source_evidence: Interest rate changes can affect a bond’s value. If bonds are held to maturity the investor will receive the face value, plus interest. If sold before maturity, the bond may be worth more or less than the face value. Rising interest rates will make newly issued bonds more appealing to investors because the newer bonds will have a higher rate of interest than older ones. To sell an older bond with a lower interest rate, you might have to sell it at a discount.
answer: Interest rate risk is the possibility that changes in interest rates affect a bond’s value. When rates rise, newly issued bonds may offer higher interest than older bonds, so an older bond may need to be sold at a discount to attract buyers. If a bond is held to maturity, the source says the investor will receive its face value plus interest; selling before maturity may result in receiving more or less than face value.
